text:
Maya: Quick brainstorm — what if the webinar narrative curve starts with a product failure story (latency spike, cost blowout) then walks through decisions that fixed it (routing, batching, quantization) so the audience feels the stakes?
Carlos: love that. start with a short customer anecdote + metric (e.g. 2x latency during peak) to make it tangible.
Rory: agree, but keep it engineering-forward. callouts: measurable before/after, rolling rollback story, and the ops playbook.
Ava: copy idea — headline hooks: 'How we kept LLM features online during 2x traffic' OR 'Make LLMs predictably cheap and fast'. we should A/B test two hooks in promo.
Maya: demo variants thought — two short demos: 1) fast micro-demo (30s) showing user flow with <200ms perceived latency, 2) deep demo (3min) showing tuning knobs: batching + cache + fallback.
Carlos: micro-demo good for socials and live run; deep demo for breakout technical audience. decide which speaker leads which.
Rory: speaker split proposal: lead product narrative = Maya, deep tuning = Ivan (ops), fallback + reliability = Sam. need to confirm Ivan is available.
Sam: I can take reliability. fallback plan: if live model latency > 1.5s/response or error rate > 2% for >30s, hot-swap to recorded clip + announce in chat. rehearse swap once.
Ava: marketing asks: 2 headline variants, 3 tweet-sized blurbs, 1 short landing hero paragraph, and UTM tagging scheme. I'll draft monday.
Maya: can someone draft two user-facing abstracts? one for exec/PM audience, one for infra/eng. keep them ~50 words.
Carlos: I'll do exec/PM. sample line: 'Practical playbook for keeping LLM features fast, reliable, and affordable as product usage scales.'
Rory: I'll draft infra/eng: mention batching, KV cache, routing policy, quantization profiles, and SLOs.
Ava: run-of-show idea — keep overall to 45 mins: 20min narrative + 10min deep demo + 10min reliability ops + 5min Q&A. propose timings below:
```
00:00 — intro + 2-line problem story (2 min)
02:00 — customer anecdote + metrics (3 min)
05:00 — product narrative & architecture sketch (10 min)
15:00 — micro-demo (3 min)
18:00 — deep demo (10 min)
28:00 — reliability & fallback playbook (7 min)
35:00 — customer case touch + next steps (5 min)
40:00 — live Q&A (5–10 min)
```
Maya: that looks tight but good. let's aim for 45 and leave buffer.
Sam: logistics — rehearsal slots: Wed 10am PT (dry run), Thu 2pm PT (tech check + recording backup). can everyone make one?
Rory: Wed OK, Thu conflict. can we swap Thu to Fri 11am PT?
Sam: Fri 11am PT works. updating calendar.
Ava: CTA variants — Register / See the playbook / Get the tuning checklist. prefer 'Get the tuning checklist' for lead magnet. add checkbox to register form for 'want follow-up pilot'.
Carlos: tracking — add utm_campaign=webinar_narrative, utm_content=hookA or hookB, and track source channel. also set a short link for A/B promo.
Maya: note for rehearsals: test the fallback swap, test recorded clip volume, and confirm captions for accessibility. also collect 3 canonical prompts for the demo so results are consistent.
Ava: can someone draft 2 subject lines for invite? I'll pick winners and schedule sends.
Rory: subject A: 'Keep LLM features fast as you scale — practical playbook'
Carlos: subject B: 'How we cut per-token cost without breaking latency'
Maya: both good. Ava: can we A/B 50/50?
Ava: yes. I'll set up A/B send with 24h spacing.
deploy-bot: Reminder: rehearsal event created; video channel reserved; recording retention = 90 days.
Maya: final asks before I wrap: Ivan confirm, 3 demo prompts, one-slide summary of fallback flow, and a short customer quote. I'll compile abstracts and draft the landing copy.
Sam: I'll send the fallback slide and confirm recorded clip by EOD Thurs.
Rory: pinging Ivan separately.
Carlos: I'll prepare exec abstract + promote plan for LinkedIn ads.
Ava: I'll draft all social hooks and the registration page tonight, share for review tomorrow morning. :rocket:
Maya: perfect — thanks team. we'll reconvene after the first rehearsal to tighten timing.
